items.title: Define a complete routine validation identity and shared trusted metadata lineage contract
items.context: Extract the exact-head/trusted-story-metadata-descendant lineage core from done-prepare validation reuse, and bind routine validation evidence to command specs and digests, configured/fallback/validate-file source, full/profile/focus, and verification policy/coverage inputs. Legacy evidence without identity is never reusable.

happy.desc: Given each supported routine validation source, when the effective plan is resolved, the stored validation identity deterministically covers source kind, normalized ordered command specs and command or entrypoint digests, full/focus/profile, plus verification policy and coverage inputs; changing none reproduces the same identity. WHY: reuse is sound only when PASS evidence names every input that can alter what validation means or executes.

Given exact-head and trusted story-metadata-descendant histories, when routine validation and DONE reuse classify lineage, both consumers return the same shared lineage result and reason. WHY: one lineage contract prevents routine validation from becoming weaker than the existing DONE trust boundary.

edge.desc: Given configured commands, fallback discovery, and validate-file execution that happen to resolve to similar text, when identities are calculated, source-specific inputs and executable digests remain represented and stable optional defaults canonicalize consistently. WHY: visually similar plans can have different trust and execution semantics.

Given a prior identity, when command order, cwd, env, timeout, config, entrypoint content, full/focus/profile, or verification policy/coverage inputs change one at a time, the identity changes; unrelated story metadata alone does not change it. WHY: every behavior-affecting delta must invalidate reuse without metadata churn causing false invalidation.

adversarial.desc: Given legacy PASS evidence with no complete validation identity, or evidence with missing, malformed, unknown-version, or partially forged identity fields, the reuse classifier rejects it and requires execution. WHY: compatibility must fail closed to real validation, never upgrade incomplete historical evidence to PASS.

Given a descendant HEAD containing any non-trusted commit among metadata commits, renamed paths, or a code/material change disguised by a trusted-looking message, shared lineage rejects metadata-descendant reuse. WHY: commit prose or endpoint hashes alone must not launder implementation changes into trusted metadata lineage.

items.title: Short-circuit fresh routine PASS validation under the execution lock
items.context: Before executeValidationPlan, read prior PASS evidence and reuse only when coverage is complete, materialHash/storyFilesHash and validation identity match, lineage is exact or trusted metadata-only, the tree is clean, and HEAD remains stable across the decision. Any read/hash/lineage/TOCTOU uncertainty falls back to real execution, never to PASS.

happy.desc: Given a clean tree and prior complete PASS evidence whose materialHash, storyFilesHash, validation identity, coverage, and exact HEAD all match, validate decides inside withValidationExecutionLock, confirms HEAD is unchanged on a second read, returns reused, and invokes zero validation commands. WHY: the common unchanged-tree case must remove redundant work without weakening serialization.

Given a clean trusted-story-metadata-descendant HEAD with unchanged material, story files, identity, and complete coverage, validate reuses the PASS under the same lock after a stable second HEAD read. WHY: metadata-only commits were the measured source of repeated full-suite waste.

edge.desc: Given concurrent validate callers, the evidence read, identity and lineage decision, both HEAD reads, and the execute-or-reuse branch occur within the existing validation execution lock so only one caller owns the decision at a time. WHY: a pre-lock freshness check would create a race even when each individual predicate is correct.

Given prior FAIL evidence, incomplete or stale coverage, dirty worktree state, mismatched material/story files/identity, or untrusted lineage, validate executes the real resolved plan and uses its result rather than returning prior PASS. WHY: reuse is an optimization and every uncertainty must fall back to the authoritative operation.

adversarial.desc: Given HEAD changes after the initial reuse checks but before return, the second HEAD read detects TOCTOU drift and forces real execution against a newly resolved or revalidated state; it never emits reused. WHY: a concurrent metadata or material commit must not make a stale decision appear atomic.

Given evidence-read, hash, git-status, lineage, identity, or HEAD-read errors and malformed values, validate handles them as explicit reuse refusals and runs validation rather than failing open to PASS. WHY: attacker-controlled or damaged metadata must be able to cost time, not manufacture success.

items.title: Expose an auditable executed-versus-reused disposition without metadata churn
items.context: Return and persist enough structured identity for future decisions while a reused result remains byte-stable: do not rewrite test-evidence, do not auto-commit metadata, and report precise refusal reasons for changed commands, config, entrypoint, focus/full/profile, policy, dirty tree, malformed evidence, untrusted lineage, or TOCTOU drift.

happy.desc: Given a real validation execution, its PASS evidence persists the complete versioned validation identity needed by a later decision and the result reports disposition executed. WHY: future reuse must be auditable from structured facts rather than reconstructed assumptions.

Given an eligible fresh PASS, validate reports disposition reused with lineage and identity basis while test-evidence bytes, git HEAD, git status, and metadata commit count remain unchanged. WHY: the shortcut only pays off if observing reuse does not itself create the next stale HEAD or evidence rewrite.

edge.desc: Given each refusal class including changed commands/config/entrypoint/full/focus/profile/policy, dirty tree, malformed or legacy evidence, incomplete coverage, untrusted lineage, and TOCTOU drift, output exposes a stable precise refusal reason and disposition executed. WHY: operators must distinguish intentional fallback from a broken reuse feature without inspecting private artifacts.

Given configured, fallback, and validate-file plans, executed evidence records the same identity schema while retaining source-specific components, and a subsequent unchanged run can consume it. WHY: auditability and reuse cannot depend on which discovery branch produced the plan.

adversarial.desc: Given a fallback execution after a failed reuse predicate, no output, receipt, or event may claim disposition reused or preserve a PASS independently of the commands actually run. WHY: mixed executed/reused reporting could let consumers treat a failing execution as cached success.

Given repeated eligible reuse calls, they remain idempotent and create no evidence rewrite, auto-commit, activity-driven material drift, or headHash churn while still returning an auditable in-memory or command result. WHY: a cache hit that mutates its cache key recreates the convergence loop this story exists to remove.

items.title: Prove safe reuse and fail-closed fallback across every validation source
items.context: Add table-driven coverage for configured commands, fallback discovery, validate-file branches, exact-head and metadata-descendant reuse, dirty tree, legacy/malformed evidence, command/config/entrypoint/full/profile/policy changes, incomplete coverage, failed prior evidence, and HEAD changes during the locked decision. Include a regression reproducing B-19ca: commands already PASS, only verificationEvidence refreshes, next validation reuses instead of running 45 commands again.

happy.desc: A table-driven suite proves first execution then zero-command reuse for configured commands, fallback discovery, and validate-file branches at exact HEAD and trusted metadata-descendant HEAD, asserting complete coverage and identical validation identity. WHY: every production source and both accepted lineage modes need the same safety guarantee.

A B-19ca regression fixture executes a 45-command PASS once, changes only checklist verificationEvidence through trusted metadata, then validates again with zero command-runner invocations and disposition reused. WHY: this reproduces the measured 32-minute waste mechanism and proves the user-visible optimization.

edge.desc: Table rows independently mutate command spec/order/digest, config source, executable entrypoint, full/focus/profile, policy/coverage inputs, materialHash, storyFilesHash, prior result, and coverage completeness; every row executes and refreshes evidence rather than reusing. WHY: one-at-a-time mutation tests reveal identity omissions hidden by broad integration scenarios.

Rows for clean exact HEAD, clean trusted metadata descendant, dirty tracked/untracked state, legacy evidence, malformed evidence, and untrusted descendant assert the expected lineage/refusal reason and command invocation count. WHY: filesystem and compatibility boundaries are common places for unsafe cache hits.

adversarial.desc: A controllable git/HEAD seam changes HEAD between the two reads inside the locked decision and proves no reuse, at least one real plan execution, and no stale PASS return; an unchanged control row proves reuse. WHY: deterministic TOCTOU coverage is required instead of relying on a flaky concurrent timing test.

Injected failures from evidence parsing, hashing, status/lineage inspection, identity resolution, and the second HEAD read each fall back to execution; if that execution fails, final result is FAIL with disposition executed. WHY: internal classifier errors must never be transformed into cached success.
